title: Hoe laat is het? — tijd, dagen, maanden
summary: Telling time, the half-zes trap, days of the week, months, and 's ochtends/'s avonds

blocks.title: Whole hours
blocks.body: Ask *Hoe laat is het?* (What time is it?). Answer with **het is … uur**. The word *uur* (o'clock / hour) never changes. For 1 o'clock, say *één uur* with the accents so it doesn't sound like 'a hour'.

blocks.title: The trap: half zes is 5:30, not 6:30
blocks.body: Here is the one that catches every learner. Dutch *half* points **forward** to the coming hour, not back. **half zes** means 'half to six' = **5:30**. So you're always naming the hour you're heading toward, one higher than the clock's big number.
blocks.callout: English 'half past five' = Dutch *half zes*. Same moment, different hour named. Trust the rule, not your instinct.

blocks.title: Quarters and minutes: over and voor
blocks.body: Use *over* (past) and *voor* (to) around the hour. **kwart over drie** = 3:15, **kwart voor vier** = 3:45. Small minutes work the same: *tien over drie* (3:10), *tien voor vier* (3:50).

blocks.explain: *half* looks forward to the next hour. 7:30 is halfway to eight, so *half acht*. *half zeven* would be 6:30.
*kwart voor acht* — a quarter to eight. *voor* = to/before.

blocks.title: The days of the week
blocks.body: Dutch week days are lowercase (no capital, unlike English). The week starts on *maandag* (Monday). *Weekend* is the same word you know, and the Dutch love it.

blocks.title: The months
blocks.body: Also lowercase, and comfortingly close to English. *maart* (March) and *mei* (May) are the ones to eyeball.

blocks.title: Parts of the day: 's ochtends, 's middags, 's avonds
blocks.body: To say 'in the morning / afternoon / evening' Dutch uses a little frozen *'s* out front. *'s ochtends* (in the morning), *'s middags* (in the afternoon), *'s avonds* (in the evening), *'s nachts* (at night). That *'s* is a shrunken old word for 'the' — just memorize the shape.
blocks.callout: *'s ochtends* and *'s morgens* both mean 'in the morning' — you'll hear both.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
Describe your week: which day is your favorite, and what time do you usually wake up? Use a part-of-day word (*'s ochtends*, *'s avonds*).
